study_identification.title: Rightward brain structural asymmetry in young children with autism

study_characteristics.study_objective: To investigate the atypical development of gray matter volume (GMV) asymmetry in individuals with ASD without DD/ID, ASD with DD/ID and individuals with only DD/ID using developmental normative models, and their associations with behavioral and clinical measures and transcription profiles.

preprocessing_pipeline.answer: CAT12; SPM12; CHN-PD (Chinese pediatric atlases); Desikan-Killiany template; 8 mm isotropic Gaussian kernel smoothing

quality_checking_detail.answer: Raw structural images were independently manually inspected by two staff members to exclude those with obvious motion artefacts. After quality control, a second round of quality control was conducted, comprising algorithms and a manual inspection of the segmentation results.

site_effect_handling_detail.answer: ComBat analysis based on an empirical Bayes approach was utilized to harmonize the site effects. Two sites: Site 1 with Philips Ingenia MRI scanner (283 children) and Site 2 with Siemens Verio MRI scanner (747 children).

response_variable.answer: GMV asymmetry (laterality index) calculated as (GMVleft - GMVright) / ((GMVleft + GMVright) / 2) for 34 brain regions based on Desikan-Killiany template

predictor_effects.answer: Age and sex were used as covariates in the GPR model. The specific modeling (fixed vs random effects) is not explicitly stated, but GPR typically treats covariates as fixed effects in the mean function.

diseases_studied.answer: Autism spectrum disorder without developmental delay/intellectual disability (ASD without DD/ID); Autism spectrum disorder with developmental delay/intellectual disability (ASD with DD/ID); Developmental delay/intellectual disability only (DD/ID)

clinical_groups_n.answer: ASD without DD/ID:212; ASD with DD/ID:563; DD/ID:36

clinical_groups_age.answer: ASD without DD/ID: 3.24±1.15 years (range 1.13-6.95); ASD with DD/ID: 3.98±1.22 years (range 1.26-6.93); DD/ID: 4.42±1.4 years (range 1.26-6.8)

deviation_metric.answer: Z-scores (individual deviations from normative model); Kurtosis of deviation values (threshold > 5 for abnormality); Standard deviation of deviation values; Skewness of deviation values

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: One-sample t-test for group-level deviation patterns (FDR corrected p < 0.05); Two-sample t-tests for between-group differences in mean values and kurtosis (FDR corrected p < 0.05); Spearman's correlation for between-group similarity with spatial permutation analysis (n=10,000) to control for spatial autocorrelation; Canonical correlation analysis (CCA) to link GMV asymmetry deviations with clinical/behavioral scores separately for ASD without DD/ID and ASD with DD/ID groups, with permutation testing (n=10,000) for significance; Partial least squares (PLS) regression to link asymmetry deviations with gene expression profiles; Inter-regional similarity analysis between gene expression and GMV asymmetry with spatial permutation tests; Unsupervised clustering (k-means and t-SNE) to explore group separability
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: ASD children (both with and without DD/ID) showed rightward GMV asymmetry in the inferior parietal lobe and precentral gyrus, and higher individual variability in the temporal pole, with ASD+DD/ID showing more extensive abnormalities linked to both ASD symptoms and verbal IQ, while ASD without DD/ID showed higher individual variability linked to ASD symptoms only.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Using normative modeling, the study found: (1) Common abnormal pattern across all ASD children: more rightward laterality in the inferior parietal lobe (ASD without DD/ID: t=-4.36, p<0.001; ASD with DD/ID: t=-4.5, p<0.001) and precentral gyrus (ASD without DD/ID: t=-4.84, p<0.001; ASD with DD/ID: t=-5.58, p<0.001), and higher individual variability in the temporal pole (kurtosis: 41.451 for ASD without DD/ID; 32.759 for ASD with DD/ID). (2) ASD with DD/ID showed severer and more extensive abnormalities including the fusiform (t=-3.9, p=0.0012), entorhinal (t=-3.4, p=0.0062), and leftward shifts in bank of superior temporal sulcus (t=2.94, p=0.022), isthmus cingulate (t=2.91, p=0.022), paracentral (t=2.82, p=0.023), and rostral anterior cingulate (t=2.8, p=0.023). (3) ASD without DD/ID showed higher individual variability in 10 regions with extreme kurtosis values (>16) including entorhinal, fusiform, medial orbitofrontal, parahippocampal, and frontal pole. (4) DD/ID children showed no significant deviations from healthy controls in asymmetry. (5) Significant spatial correlation was found between ASD with DD/ID vs. ASD without DD/ID (r=0.557, permuted p=0.0007) and between ASD with DD/ID vs. DD/ID (r=0.741, permuted p<0.0001). (6) For ASD without DD/ID, CCA identified one significant mode linking GMV asymmetry with clinical scores (r=0.977, pperm=0.033), positively associated with ADOS scores and visual responsiveness. (7) For ASD with DD/ID, CCA identified one significant mode linking asymmetry with both clinical and IQ scores (r=0.988, pperm=0.003), associated with verbal IQ, operation, self-management, and ASD symptoms. (8) Inter-regional similarity analysis revealed significant associations between gene expression profiles and GMV asymmetry deviations for all three patient groups (ASD with DD/ID: r=0.16, pperm=0.0001; ASD without DD/ID: r=0.216, pperm=0; DD/ID: r=0.241, pperm=0). (9) Gene enrichment analysis identified four GO terms consistently enriched across all patient groups: 'regulation of transmembrane transport', 'neuron projection development', 'axon', and 'supramolecular fiber organization'.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: First, GMV was obtained by automated voxel-based morphometry (VBM), and the performances of segmentation and registration in preprocessing are key factors affecting VBM accuracy. Second, the normative model only considered age and sex effects, not environmental factors such as socioeconomic status. Third, gene expression data from healthy adults were used to link with GMV asymmetry in 1-7 year-old children, requiring multivariate rather than univariate association methods. Fourth, the sex ratio was unbalanced (predominantly male), limiting exploration of sex effects on developmental disorders. Fifth, most subjects (especially patient groups) were scanned during sedation-induced sleep, with higher sedation proportions in ASD and DD/ID groups compared to TD, which might confound results. Finally, functional brain variants were not included in the multiscale cascade analysis.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: The study demonstrates the utility of normative modeling in capturing individual-level deviations rather than group-level differences, which may be particularly important given the high heterogeneity in ASD. The authors suggest that brain asymmetry has potential as an intermediate neural phenotype linking genetic factors and clinical manifestations for these atypical populations. The findings indicate that brain GMV asymmetry patterns might be gradually differentiated along a continuum across ASD without DD/ID, ASD with DD/ID, and DD/ID groups, rather than forming distinct subtypes. The normative modeling approach with deviations successfully captured specific alterations in brain structure laterality of young ASD children that previous group-level analyses had failed to detect consistently.
